label: lem:orthogonal-semisimple-trivial-borel
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:orthogonal-semisimple-trivial-borel}
If $A\leq P_1$ and every semisimple image of $A$ in the successive Levi quotients of singular line stabilizers is trivial, then $A$ lies in a Borel subgroup of $G$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For the chosen singular line $\ell$, the image of $A$ on $W=\ell^\perp/\ell$ lies in the diagonal quotient, so modulo $R_u(P_1)$ the image of $A$ acts projectively by scalars on $W$ and stabilizes every singular subspace of $W$. We choose a singular line $M$ of $W$ and lift it to a totally singular plane of $V$ containing $\ell$. This plane is the inverse image of $M$ under the quotient map $\ell^\perp\to W$. Repeating the operation of lifting a singular line to extend the stabilized flag in $V$, we build a complete totally singular flag stabilized by $A$. More explicitly, this flag is $0=F_0<F_1<\cdots<F_r$, where $\dim F_i=i$ for $0\leq i\leq r$ and $r$ is the Witt index of $V$. Each $F_i$ is totally singular, and $F_r$ is maximal totally singular. The Witt index drops at each step. Since the totally singular flag constructed in this way is complete, its stabilizer in $G$ is a Borel subgroup of $G$ \cite{Carter1985}, \cite[Proposition 26.1(b)]{MalleTesterman2011}.

label: lem:pgu4-borel-interface
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pgu4-borel-interface}
Let $\operatorname{PSU}_4(q)\leq E\leq\operatorname{PGU}_4(q)$, and let $B_E$ be the normalizer in $E$ of a Borel subgroup of $\operatorname{PSU}_4(q)$. If $C\leq B_E$ is hereditarily $E$-permutable, then the image of $C$ in the unitary socle of $E$ is trivial. Moreover, the remaining diagonal image is the image of $C$ in $E/\operatorname{PSU}_4(q)$, and it is toral. This toral image is considered when taking the intersection of the kernels of the projective actions on the spaces $W_i$ in {\rm Theorem \ref{thm:orthogonal-borel}}.

title: Proof
body_md:
For $q=2$, the quotient $\operatorname{PGU}_4(2)/\operatorname{PSU}_4(2)$ is trivial \cite[p. 66]{Wilson2009} and $\operatorname{PSU}_4(2)\cong\operatorname{PSp}_4(3)$ \cite[\S3.6.5]{Wilson2009}, so Theorem \ref{thm:symplectic} proves the conclusion. Assume that $q\geq3$. The relative root system of rank two of $\operatorname{SU}_4(q)$ is of type $\mathcal{C}_2$. We use the relative root system for ${}^2A_3$ \cite{Carter1985} and the finite Levi quotients \cite[Proposition 26.1(b)]{MalleTesterman2011}. With simple relative roots $\alpha,\beta$, the positive roots are
$$
        \alpha,~\beta,~\alpha+\beta,~2\alpha+\beta.
$$
The two maximal parabolics of $E$ containing $B_E$ have Levi quotients of rank one of type $\operatorname{PSU}_2(q)\leq E_1\leq\operatorname{PGU}_2(q)$ or $\operatorname{PSL}_2(q^2)\leq E_2\leq\operatorname{PGL}_2(q^2)$, with $\operatorname{PSU}_2(q)\cong\operatorname{PSL}_2(q)$ \cite[p. 66]{Wilson2009}. By Lemma \ref{lem:quotient-inheritance}, the images of $C$ in $E_1$ and $E_2$ are hereditarily $E_i$-permutable and lie in Borel subgroups of the respective quotients. Since $q\geq3$, Lemma \ref{lem:pgl2-borel} shows that both images corresponding to the simple roots are trivial.

Hence the components corresponding to the simple roots and the two toral characters vanish, and the remaining possible image of $C$ lies in the product of the two root subgroups corresponding to $\alpha+\beta$ and $2\alpha+\beta$. As in Lemma \ref{lem:symplectic-c2-borel}, the roots $2\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha+\beta$ occur in Levi factors of rank one after we conjugate these two parabolics of $E$ by the simple reflections. In these Levi factors of rank one, Lemma \ref{lem:quotient-inheritance} with Lemma \ref{lem:pgl2-borel} shows that both components of the image of $C$ corresponding to these two positive roots are trivial. So the image of $C$ in the unitary socle is trivial, and any diagonal toral image of $C$ is treated in Theorem \ref{thm:orthogonal-borel}.

label: thm:orthogonal-borel
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:orthogonal-borel}
Let $G=\mathrm{P}\Omega(V)$ be of type $B_m$, $D_m^+$, or $D_m^-$, and let $B$ be a Borel subgroup of this orthogonal group. If $A\leq B$ is hereditarily $G$-permutable, then $A=1$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We induct on $\dim V$. The quotients $W_i$ associated with singular line stabilizers have dimension $\dim V-2$. The bases are the cases in dimension at most six identified by the isomorphisms \eqref{eq:orthogonal-low-rank-isomorphisms}, $\mathrm{P}\Omega_5\cong\operatorname{PSp}_4$, $\mathrm{P}\Omega_6^+\cong\operatorname{PSL}_4$, $\mathrm{P}\Omega_6^-\cong\operatorname{PSU}_4$, $\mathrm{P}\Omega_4^-\cong\operatorname{PSL}_2(q^2)$, and the group of rank one $\mathrm{P}\Omega_3\cong\operatorname{PSL}_2(q)$. These are settled by Theorems \ref{thm:split-linear}, \ref{thm:unitary}, \ref{thm:symplectic} and the known result for $\operatorname{PSL}_2$. In particular, this includes their $q=2$ instances ($\operatorname{PSp}_4(2)$, $\operatorname{PSL}_4(2)\cong A_8$, $\operatorname{PSU}_4(2)$). Since $\mathrm{P}\Omega_{2m+1}(2)\cong\operatorname{PSp}_{2m}(2)$ is symplectic, for type $B_m$ we take $q$ odd. So we assume that $\dim V\geq7$, whence the Witt index is $r\geq3$. Let $E$ be the maximal totally singular subspace of $V$ whose complete flag is stabilized by $B$. This flag is $0=F_0<F_1<\cdots<F_r=E$, with $\dim F_i=i$ for $0\leq i\leq r$. Each $F_i$ is totally singular, and the flag ends at $E$ of dimension $r$. We take a Witt decomposition \cite[pp. 26--39]{KleidmanLiebeck1990}
$$
        V=E\oplus D\oplus E^*,~ E=\langle e_1,\ldots,e_r\rangle,~ E^*=\langle f_r,\ldots,f_1\rangle,
$$
with $D=0$ (even dimension of plus type), $D=\langle d\rangle$ an anisotropic line (odd dimension), or $D$ an anisotropic plane (even dimension of minus type). The vectors $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ are chosen so that $F_i=\langle e_1,\ldots,e_i\rangle$ for $1\leq i\leq r$.

We consider the stabilizer $P_E$ of $E$ in $G$ and the projective factor of its Levi quotient acting on $E$. We form this projective factor by taking the quotient of the Levi quotient by the kernel of its projective action on $E$. Write $\rho_E$ for this projective action of the Levi quotient of $P_E$ on $E$. The projective factor is the image of $\rho_E$. This quotient has linear socle $\operatorname{PSL}(E)\cong\operatorname{PSL}_r(q)$ with toral and anisotropic factors \cite[Proposition 26.1(b)]{MalleTesterman2011}. The image of $A$ lies in a Borel subgroup of this Levi quotient. Therefore, Lemma \ref{lem:sl-borel} shows that this image of $A$ is trivial. In particular, the group $A$ acts projectively by scalars on $E$ and stabilizes each $\langle e_i\rangle$.

For each $i$ let $W_i=\langle e_i\rangle^\perp/\langle e_i\rangle$. We have $A\leq P_{\langle e_i\rangle}$, where this parabolic is the stabilizer of $\langle e_i\rangle$ in $G$. By Lemma \ref{lem:quotient-inheritance}, the image of $A$ is hereditarily permutable in the orthogonal quotient of this stabilizer acting on $W_i$. The quotient is again a projective orthogonal quotient \cite[Proposition 26.1(b)]{MalleTesterman2011}, and the image of $A$ lies in its induced Borel subgroup. By induction on $\dim V$, the image of $A$ in each orthogonal quotient whose space has dimension greater than six is trivial. For the quotients of low rank reached at the end of the descent, we use Lemma \ref{lem:pgl2-borel}, Lemma \ref{lem:sl-borel}, Theorem \ref{thm:symplectic-borel}, and the $\operatorname{PGU}_4(q)$ case of Lemma \ref{lem:pgu4-borel-interface} for the minus case in dimension six. The plus case in dimension four gives two quotients of rank one, handled by Lemma \ref{lem:pgl2-borel}. Any diagonal or toral part is left to the intersection of the kernels of the projective actions on all the spaces $W_i$. So the orthogonal image of $A$ on $W_i$ is trivial for each $i$.

It remains to determine the intersection of the kernels of the projective actions on the spaces $W_i$. In the standard root notation \cite{Carter1985} and with a Witt basis as in \cite[pp. 26--39]{KleidmanLiebeck1990}, the root subgroups involving two coordinates have supports corresponding to the roots $e_i-e_j$ and $e_i+e_j$ ($i<j$). In odd dimension there are groups corresponding to short roots with support $e_i$, and in even dimension of minus type the root subgroups involving $D$ also have support on one coordinate. A root subgroup involving the coordinates indexed by $a$ and $b$ acts nontrivially on $W_i$ for some $i\notin\{a,b\}$ (possible as $r\geq3$). Similarly, a root subgroup involving only the coordinate indexed by $a$ acts nontrivially on some $W_i$ with $i\neq a$. Hence all unipotent components vanish. For the toral part of $A$, the projective factor of the Levi quotient of $P_E$ acting on $E$ shows that $A$ acts on $E$ as a single projective scalar, so $e_i\mapsto\lambda e_i$ for all $i$. The dual flag in $E^*$ has terms $F_j^*=\langle f_r,\ldots,f_{r-j+1}\rangle$ for $1\leq j\leq r$. Since the elements of $A$ leave the values of the quadratic form unchanged and stabilize the dual flag, we have $f_i\mapsto\lambda^{-1}f_i$. The anisotropic part $D$ lies in $\langle e_i\rangle^\perp$ for every $i$ and meets $\langle e_i\rangle$ trivially, so $D$ embeds in each $W_i$. Since the orthogonal image of $A$ on $W_i$ is trivial, $A$ acts on $W_i$, and hence on $D\subseteq W_i$, as a scalar. Write $\nu_i$ for the scalar on $W_i$ and $\mu$ for the scalar by which $A$ acts on $D$. In the standard coordinate description of a maximal torus of the orthogonal group of $V$ \cite[p. 70]{Wilson2009}, an element in all the kernels for the projective actions on the spaces $W_i$ is, modulo the projective centre,
$$
        e_i\mapsto\lambda e_i,~ f_i\mapsto\lambda^{-1}f_i~(1\leq i\leq r),~ x\mapsto\mu x~(x\in D).
$$
The hyperbolic pair $e_j,f_j$ ($j\neq i$) inside $W_i$ shows that $\nu_i=\lambda=\lambda^{-1}$, so $\lambda^2=1$, while the image of $D$ in $W_i$ shows that $\nu_i=\mu$, hence $\mu=\lambda$. In odd dimension $\det A=\mu$, so $A\in\operatorname{SO}(V)$ forces $\mu=1$. Therefore, $\lambda=1$ and hence $A=1$. By contrast, in even dimension of minus type $\mu=\lambda=\pm1$, so $A$ acts as the scalar $\lambda$ on all of $V$ and is projectively trivial. In particular, the action on the anisotropic plane is projectively trivial. The case of even dimension and plus type ($D=0$) is identical with no anisotropic part. For each of these three orthogonal types, the kernels for the projective actions on all the spaces $W_i$ intersect in projective scalars. Hence $A=1$.

title: Proof
body_md: The cases of low rank in \eqref{eq:orthogonal-low-rank-isomorphisms} are handled by Theorems \ref{thm:split-linear}, \ref{thm:unitary} and \ref{thm:symplectic} and the base of rank one. Otherwise, let $A<G$ be proper, nontrivial, and hereditarily $G$-permutable. By the alternatives obtained from hereditary permutability with the singular line stabilizer $P_1$, the factorization case $G = A P_1 ^x$ is impossible (Proposition \ref{prop:orthogonal-no-p1-factorization}), so $A\leq P_1$ after conjugating $A$ in $G$. The image of $A$ on $W = \ell^\perp/\ell$ is governed by Lemma \ref{lem:orthogonal-actual-levi-alternatives}. A proper nontrivial semisimple image $C$ of $A$ lies in a proper parabolic of the Levi quotient of the singular line stabilizer in that descent step, so $A$ lies in the corresponding smaller parabolic of $G$ and the flag stabilized by $A$ extends in the descent. The case in which the semisimple image of $A$ is full cannot occur (Lemma \ref{lem:orthogonal-full-levi-obstruction}). If the semisimple image of $A$ is trivial, then $A$ is contained in a Borel subgroup of $G$ (Lemma \ref{lem:orthogonal-semisimple-trivial-borel}). In this case, $A$ is trivial by Theorem \ref{thm:orthogonal-borel}. So $A=1$.

title: Proof
body_md: By the classification of finite simple groups, a finite simple group is cyclic of prime order, alternating, classical, exceptional of Lie type (including the Tits group), or sporadic. Since $G$ is nonabelian, the cyclic case cannot occur. The alternating groups are covered by Vasil'ev and Tyutyanov \cite{VT2012}. For the sporadic groups and the Tits group, we use the result of Galt and Tyutyanov \cite[Corollary]{GT2022}. Galt and Tyutyanov \cite[Theorem 1 and Proposition 1]{GT2023} also obtained the required conclusion for the exceptional groups of Lie type and the groups $\operatorname{PSL}_2(q)$. The groups $\operatorname{PSU}_3(q)$ are covered by Theorem \ref{thm:unitary-low-bases}, with \cite[Theorem 2]{GT2025} as the source for $q\geq3$. The remaining classical groups of higher rank are covered by the four theorems proved in this paper, namely $\operatorname{PSL}_n(q)$ by Theorem \ref{thm:split-linear}, $\operatorname{PSU}_n(q)$ by Theorem \ref{thm:unitary}, $\operatorname{PSp}_{2m}(q)$ by Theorem \ref{thm:symplectic}, and $\mathrm{P}\Omega(V)$ by Theorem \ref{thm:orthogonal}. Hence $G$ has no proper nontrivial hereditarily $G$-permutable subgroup.
